launch-ga-atlanta-piedmont-park.description: Lake Clara Meer is the central water landmark, with skyline views, paved paths, fishing areas, and nearby lawns; swimming is not allowed.
Noguchi Playscape is the landmark sculptural playground near a listed restroom; route to it directly rather than using the general park pin.
Legacy Fountain is the free seasonal splash pad, separate from the paid pool and subject to weather, events, maintenance, and seasonal hours.
The seasonal Aquatic Center has beach entry, lap lanes, current channel, locker rooms, showers, concessions, and a separate admission fee.
The fenced dog areas sit below the Park Drive bridge, with separate spaces, water, shade, benches, and a nearby restroom.
Active Oval concentrates the running loop, sports fields, sand volleyball, and fitness activity; scheduled use can limit casual access.

launch-ga-atlanta-centennial-olympic-par.description: The Fountain of Rings is the park's signature landmark, with scheduled daily shows that may pause for weather, maintenance, or events.
Paralympic Legacy Plaza interprets Atlanta's 1996 Paralympic history and provides a useful orientation point in the park.
The Quilt of Nations displays flags of the countries represented in the 1996 Games and sits along the park's memorial landscape.
The Southern Company Amphitheater hosts programmed performances and events; access can be controlled during setup and ticketed activity.
The Visitor Center and Olympic Rings make a practical meeting point for first-time visitors exploring surrounding downtown attractions.

launch-ga-atlanta-historic-fourth-ward-p.description: The two-acre lake is working stormwater infrastructure and a scenic centerpiece, not a swimming or wading area.
The free seasonal splash pad is listed for 10 a.m.-8 p.m. May 1 through October 1, subject to weather and maintenance.
The shaded playground sits in the upper Dallas Street section near the splash pad, making this the best family arrival point.
The amphitheater and great lawn host community programs and provide open gathering space above the basin.
The skatepark occupies the southern section near the BeltLine and a listed accessible public restroom.
The Eastside Trail connection links the park to Ponce City Market, Piedmont Park, Inman Park, and Krog Street.

launch-ga-atlanta-grant-park.description: The main playground provides neighborhood family play within the shaded historic park; use the closest street entrance.
Grant Park Recreation Center has its own staffed schedule and programs, separate from general park hours.
The outdoor pool is seasonal and uses City aquatics hours, fees, weather rules, and capacity limits.
Zoo Atlanta is inside the broader park landscape but is a separately ticketed attraction with dedicated entrances and parking.
Sports fields support soccer, baseball, kickball, football, and ultimate; permitted games take priority.
The picnic pavilion offers reservable cover; city rules apply to grills, tents, amplified sound, alcohol, and organized gatherings.

launch-ga-atlanta-westside-park.description: The grand overlook frames the protected reservoir and city skyline; it is a viewpoint, not a water-access area.
The Birth of Atlanta sculpture and monumental gateway form the park's most recognizable arrival sequence.
The playground sits beyond the main parking areas, so families should expect a walk and bring needed supplies.
The Johnson Road entrance is the most useful common arrival for central lawns, playground routes, and overlooks.
The paved reservoir loop provides long exposed walking and cycling segments with significant distances and grades.
The Bellwood Quarry overlook explains the site's industrial history while keeping visitors behind reservoir safety barriers.

launch-ga-atlanta-chastain-park.description: The central playground is a free family destination near West Wieuca Road and separate from ticketed or staffed facilities.
The PATH loop circles much of the park and crosses facility drives; walkers should stay alert at access points.
The tennis center is a staffed facility with court reservations, fees, and hours separate from the park.
The seasonal public pool has separate admission, aquatics rules, weather closures, and operating hours.
The amphitheater is a ticketed event venue whose concerts can alter roads, parking, noise, and park access.
North Fulton Golf Course occupies a large portion of the park and is not general pedestrian lawn space.

launch-ga-atlanta-freedom-park.description: Freedom Park Trail is the main paved spine linking neighborhoods, art, the Carter Center, and BeltLine connections.
The Carter Center overlook provides broad views, but museum access, parking, and hours are separate from the park.
The Bridge sculpture marks the park's civic history and is one stop in a wider outdoor art collection.
Permanent and temporary sculptures are spread across multiple park segments rather than contained in one garden.
The Moreland Avenue meadow is a visible open segment near Little Five Points, with busy road crossings nearby.
The Eastside Trail junction provides a practical connection toward Ponce, Piedmont Park, Inman Park, and Krog Street.

launch-ga-atlanta-eastside-trail.description: The Piedmont Park connection is the northern anchor and provides access to park restrooms, lawns, lake, and family facilities.
Ponce City Market is a busy private mixed-use access point with food, paid parking, elevators, and heavy trail traffic.
Historic Fourth Ward Park access leads to the lake, playground, seasonal splash pad, skatepark, and public restroom.
The Freedom Park Trail junction branches east through public art and neighborhood greenways toward the Carter Center.
Krog Street Market is a popular southern access and food stop, with private operating hours and limited parking.
Krog Street Tunnel and Wylie Street are known for changing street art; stay alert around road crossings and active traffic.

launch-ga-atlanta-cascade-springs-nature.description: Cascade Falls is reached on a wooded trail; rocks and creek edges can be extremely slippery, especially after rain.
The moss-covered historic springhouse is a signature landmark reached from the main trail network.
Boardwalk sections improve passage over wet ground but do not make every natural trail or landmark step-free.
The Utoy Creek trail moves through shaded forest with roots, mud, water edges, and changing conditions.
Historic earthworks remain in the forest; protect the site by staying on established paths.
The outdoor amphitheater is a rustic gathering area, not a guaranteed weather shelter or staffed facility.

launch-ga-atlanta-perkerson-park.description: The free seasonal splash pad shares the family zone with the playground and may close for weather, maintenance, or season.
The playground includes separate age areas, resilient surfacing, and ramp access on the toddler structure.
The wooded disc-golf course crosses uneven terrain; players and other visitors should watch for flying discs.
Tennis courts are available for play when not reserved or programmed and follow facility rules.
The pavilion supports reserved gatherings and shade near family amenities; reservation and event rules apply.
Sports fields support community play and permitted programs; organized use takes priority over casual activity.
